article.headline: Games To Watch: Perfect district starts meet at Seminary and Falkner
article.html:
Perfect district records meet at Seminary and Falkner on Thursday night. Magee visits Seminary with both teams 3–0 in league play, while Potts Camp and Falkner bring matching 2–0 district starts into their meeting. Those direct tests lead the October 29 Games To Watch, with unbeaten soccer teams and a pair of winning girls basketball openers adding interest before the night is over. All times below are CDT.

Football: long winning runs meet at Seminary

Magee is 7–1 and Seminary 8–1 entering their 7 p.m. district game at Seminary. Both have won six straight, and neither has lost a district game. The combination makes this more than a comparison of strong overall records: the teams bring equally unblemished league starts and sustained winning form directly against one another.

At Falkner, the 7 p.m. meeting with Potts Camp offers another matchup of unbeaten district records. Potts Camp enters 5–2 overall and Falkner 5–3, but each is 2–0 in league games. Their overall paths differ; their district starts do not. This game provides a direct comparison between those two winning league records.

Football: matching records in Maben and Glen

Eupora travels to East Webster for a 7 p.m. kickoff in Maben. Both enter 8–1 overall and 2–1 in district play. The appeal is that close alignment across both measures: each has put together a strong season, and each reaches this conference meeting with the same number of district wins and losses.

Kossuth visits Alcorn Central in Glen at 7 p.m., with both 2–1 in district play. Kossuth is 5–3 overall and Central 5–4. Alcorn County Sports reports that the Aggies bring two consecutive wins into Central’s senior night, while the Golden Bears have lost two straight. Those different recent runs give their matching league records a sharper context.

Girls soccer: unbeaten starts face fresh tests

Itawamba Agricultural visits Caledonia at 5 p.m., with both teams listed at 1–0. Caledonia’s current totals show six goals scored and none conceded; Itawamba’s show three scored and one allowed. Each has an opening win, making this an early test against another side that has already found a winning result.

Sumrall takes a 3–0 record to St. Martin, which is 1–0, for a 5:30 p.m. match in Ocean Springs. Neither has conceded in its posted results: Sumrall has scored 12 goals and St. Martin seven. That gives the meeting a clear point of interest, with two productive attacks facing defenses that have kept every reported opponent off the scoreboard.

Boys soccer: Hernando, Starkville and Biloxi test winning starts

Hernando visits Starkville at 7 p.m., with both entering 1–0. Hernando’s posted totals are five goals for and none against; Starkville’s are three for and one against. Their nonconference meeting gives each a second recorded test against a team that also opened with a victory.

Biloxi hosts St. Stanislaus at 7:30 p.m.. The Indians are 3–0 with six goals scored and none conceded, while the Rock-a-Chaws enter 2–1. Biloxi’s latest result was a 1–0 win at Long Beach on Tuesday, covered in our Tuesday results roundup. St. Stanislaus brings a winning record of its own into that test of Biloxi’s clean-sheet start.

Girls basketball: St. Joseph Catholic and Leake Academy meet unbeaten

St. Joseph Catholic of Madison meets Leake Academy of Madden in a neutral-site game at 7:15 p.m.. Both enter 1–0 after decisive Tuesday wins: the Bruins beat Manchester Academy 53–27, and Leake won 72–13 at Canton Academy. The opening results supply the reason to watch this next step: two teams that began with clear victories now face another unbeaten opponent.
